coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Planning permission runs through the Development Control Authority under the Physical Planning Act 2003, which keeps a register of permits. No contractor registration, accreditation or local-content reporting regime was found, and no inland quarry permit rules.

result.competitor: I found no villa- or short-term-rental-specific ABST or levy filing software or service. IRD forms appear to be PDF downloads paid through local banks; I found no confirmed online filing portal. Risk: the 2026 budget (KPMG) plans full ABST digitisation, e-invoicing and a new tax administration platform, which may absorb filing. Local accountants and property managers likely file by hand for owners (not verified).
result.duty: ABST registration is mandatory once a property provides accommodation for up to 45 days. This is the IRD's statement as reported by the Antigua Observer in Feb 2026; the article fetch returned 403 and I read it only through search snippets. Returns are monthly: the IRD says the 15th, while a third-party form guide says the last day of the following month. Late penalty is reported as $500 or 5% of tax due, whichever is greater, or 5% per month plus interest (third-party sources). Tourism Accommodation Levy Act 2021: US$3 per guest per night up to a US$150 room rate, US$5 above that; it covers hotels, guest houses, private villas and Airbnbs; a return is due within 21 days after each payment period, aligned with the ABST period if registered. Conflicts not resolved: the accommodation ABST rate (17% standard since 1 Jan 2024; some guides list 12.5% for hotels and 10.5% for holiday accommodation), and a third-party guide's EC$300,000 registration threshold versus the IRD's 45-day statement. Airbnb does not appear to collect or remit; the 2017 Airbnb announcement only began a dialogue on taxation.
result.market: Very small. A 2023 Observer report (via search summary) said fewer than 300 of about 500 Airbnb-listed properties were registered with the government. Third-party data put listings at roughly 1,000 or more. I found no official count of licensed villas or guest houses.
result.reason: The duty is real. In Feb 2026 the IRD said ABST registration and returns are mandatory for villas and Airbnbs. The 2021 Tourism Accommodation Levy (US$3/US$5 per guest per night) covers private villas and Airbnbs, with a return due within 21 days of each period. I found no villa-specific filing tool, and no confirmed IRD e-filing portal. But a new tax administration platform and ABST e-invoicing are planned in the 2026 budget, and a state-built system could take over the core job. The market is tiny: about 500 Airbnb listings in 2023, under 300 registered. Many hosts don't comply, so they won't pay for compliance. ABST rate (17%, 12.5% or 10.5%) and threshold (EC$300k vs 45 days) are unresolved. Airbnb does not remit (2017 dialogue only).

decisions.reason: Villa and short-term rental hosts filing ABST and guest levy is a new buyer and duty versus K01 e-invoicing.
Annual work-permit renewal by employers is a different duty from K02 household payroll levy.
Pesticide importer and applicator licensing is a small-firm recurring duty and in scope; the small market is for verifiers.
Co-operatives and credit unions are in-scope bodies with annual returns to the Supervisor.
Pharmacies are in-scope small professional offices with licence and register duties.
Small companies and registered agents have recurring annual return and beneficial ownership filings, a new duty.
Licensed cannabis operators have mandatory recurring reporting; small buyer count is for verifiers.
Yacht agents and charter operators are a different buyer from K04 ship agents; related K04, no revival evidence claimed.
Tour operators collecting ABST from 1 Sept 2026 is a different buyer and duty from K01; related K01.
Clinic licensing is a small professional office duty; bill status is unverified, so verifiers decide.
Nursery and childcare licensing and inspection is a recurring duty on small operators.
Central Board of Health food permits are a different buyer and duty from K07 Heritage Quay vendor registration.
Equipment inspection certificates would be a recurring duty on small owners; existence unverified, so keep.
Scrap yard and derelict vehicle permits are unverified; unsure, so keep for verification.
Jewellers' AML registration under ONDCP is the same DNFBP AML duty as K05.
